concepts.name: Background and Context of the Gandhi-Irwin Pact
key_dimensions: Role of Civil Disobedience Movement (1930) as the immediate precursor
Significance of Salt March (Dandi March) in creating political leverage for Gandhi
Viceroy Irwin's conciliatory approach vs. hardliner British opposition (Churchill's criticism)
Role of Tej Bahadur Sapru and M.R. Jayakar as intermediaries in initiating negotiations

concepts.name: Formal Details and Signatories of the Pact
key_dimensions: Date of signing: March 5, 1931 — UPSC trap on confusing with Round Table Conference dates
Parties: Mahatma Gandhi (INC) and Lord Irwin (Viceroy) — not the British Parliament
It was an agreement, NOT a treaty — legal status and its implications
Gandhi's designation as sole representative of INC and the controversy therein

concepts.name: Key Provisions: INC Concessions to the British
key_dimensions: Suspension (not withdrawal) of Civil Disobedience Movement — UPSC trap on 'suspension vs. withdrawal'
INC agreed to participate in Second Round Table Conference
Discontinuation of boycott of British goods (partial relaxation)
Return of confiscated properties not yet sold — conditionality aspect

concepts.name: Key Provisions: British Concessions to INC
key_dimensions: Release of political prisoners arrested during Civil Disobedience (exception: those convicted of violence)
Withdrawal of emergency ordinances promulgated during CDM
Permission to collect/manufacture salt in coastal villages for personal use — not for trade
Remission of fines not yet collected from satyagrahis

concepts.name: The Salt Satyagraha Clause: Scope and Limitations
key_dimensions: Right to collect salt from natural deposits ONLY along coastline — inland salt monopoly retained
Salt tax was NOT abolished — a common misconception and UPSC trap
Limited to personal consumption, not commercial exploitation
Contrast with Gandhi's original demand for complete abolition of salt tax

concepts.name: The Question of Political Prisoners: What Was NOT Conceded
key_dimensions: British refused to release those convicted of violence — Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, Sukhdev explicitly excluded
Gandhi's failure to secure commutation of death sentences — major criticism of the pact
Distinction between 'political prisoners' and 'prisoners of violence' as a British framing device
HSRA's (Hindustan Socialist Republican Association) condemnation of the pact

concepts.name: Bhagat Singh Controversy and Gandhi's Role
key_dimensions: Bhagat Singh hanged on March 23, 1931 — just 18 days after the pact
Gandhi's intercession on behalf of Bhagat Singh: did it happen and was it sincere? — historiographical debate
Revolutionary nationalists' accusation that Gandhi 'traded' Bhagat Singh for the pact
Impact on Gandhi's popularity and INC's image among youth and radical sections

concepts.name: Gandhi as INC's Sole Representative at Second Round Table Conference
key_dimensions: Karachi Session (1931) ratified the pact AND authorized Gandhi as sole INC delegate — sequence matters
Irony: Gandhi was the only INC representative surrounded by communal and princely interests
Failure of Second RTC and its direct connection to resumption of CDM in 1932
Contrast with First RTC (INC absent) and Third RTC (INC absent again after pact collapse)

concepts.name: Karachi Session of INC (1931): Ratification and Resolutions
key_dimensions: Presided over by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel — not Gandhi, a common UPSC confusion
Passed the Fundamental Rights and Economic Policy Resolution alongside pact ratification
Karachi Resolution on Fundamental Rights seen as INC's alternative socio-economic vision
Protest against Bhagat Singh's execution registered even while ratifying the pact — dual messaging

concepts.name: Criticism of the Gandhi-Irwin Pact from Within the Nationalist Movement
key_dimensions: Left wing (Nehru, Bose) criticized it as surrender of revolutionary momentum
Revolutionary nationalists (HSRA) saw it as betrayal of Bhagat Singh
Muslim League and communal groups felt INC negotiated only for Hindu interests
Debate: Was it a 'truce between equals' or 'unequal compromise'? — Irwin's characterization

concepts.name: Defence of the Gandhi-Irwin Pact: Strategic Rationale
key_dimensions: Gave INC a breathing space to reorganize after massive repression of CDM
First time a Viceroy negotiated with an Indian leader as an equal — symbolic significance
Secured release of tens of thousands of political prisoners
Demonstrated INC's capacity to bring British administration to the negotiating table

concepts.name: Lord Irwin's Position and the British Political Context
key_dimensions: Irwin's belief in dominion status (Irwin Declaration 1929) as context for his conciliatory approach
Churchill's famous 'half-naked fakir' statement as opposition to the pact
Irwin replaced by Lord Willingdon — hardliner — leading to collapse of pact's spirit
Simon Commission backdrop: pact seen as British attempt to include INC in constitutional process

concepts.name: Collapse of the Gandhi-Irwin Pact and Resumption of CDM
key_dimensions: Failure of Second Round Table Conference (Sep–Dec 1931) due to communal deadlock
Lord Willingdon's refusal to meet Gandhi on return — immediate trigger for CDM resumption
Gandhi's arrest in January 1932 and promulgation of new ordinances
Poona Pact (1932) as a separate but connected subsequent development — UPSC overlap trap

concepts.name: Comparison: Gandhi-Irwin Pact vs. Lucknow Pact (1916)
key_dimensions: Lucknow Pact: INC–Muslim League agreement; Gandhi-Irwin: INC–British Government agreement
Both represented tactical compromises rather than ideological alignments
Lucknow Pact's separate electorate concession vs. Gandhi-Irwin's silence on communal question
Both failed to achieve long-term objectives — UPSC comparative question angle

concepts.name: The Pact's Silence on Key Demands: What Was NOT Addressed
key_dimensions: No mention of Purna Swaraj (complete independence) — INC's 1929 Lahore Resolution demand
No constitutional reforms promised — the pact was purely about suspension of agitation
Agrarian distress issues of peasants not substantively addressed
No commitment on future of Simon Commission recommendations or federation proposals

concepts.name: Impact on the Civil Disobedience Movement: Suspension vs. Withdrawal Dynamics
key_dimensions: Suspension kept CDM as a 'threat in reserve' — strategic ambiguity
Mass mobilization's psychological impact diluted during the truce period
Provincial Congress Committees' difficulty in controlling local agitations after suspension
Pattern repeated in 1934 when CDM was finally withdrawn — compare the two decisions

concepts.name: Role of the Pact in India's Constitutional Progression
key_dimensions: INC's participation in Second RTC influenced debates leading to Government of India Act 1935
Gandhi's insistence on representing 'all Indians' foreshadowed future INC–League conflict
British use of communal representation at RTC as a counterweight to INC's claims
Pact legitimized INC as THE representative body — both its strength and source of communal tension

concepts.name: Historiographical Interpretations of the Gandhi-Irwin Pact
key_dimensions: Nationalist historiography (Nehru's autobiography): pact as necessary but imperfect tactical step
Subaltern Studies perspective: voices of workers, peasants, revolutionaries marginalized in the deal
Revisionist view: Gandhi secured maximum possible given INC's weakened organizational state post-repression
Colonial archives perspective: British viewed it as successfully 'splitting' moderates from radicals

concepts.name: Gandhi-Irwin Pact and the Question of Equality in Negotiation
key_dimensions: Irwin's statement: 'I was negotiating with a man who had shaken the British Empire' — symbolic parity
First instance of a non-official Indian being treated as an equal by the Crown's representative
Contrast with Morley-Minto and Montagu-Chelmsford reforms — top-down British grants vs. negotiated agreement
Set precedent for future negotiations (Cabinet Mission, Mountbatten Plan) — negotiation as method

concepts.name: Relationship Between Gandhi-Irwin Pact and the Poona Pact (1932): Linkages and Distinctions
key_dimensions: Gandhi-Irwin: INC vs. British; Poona Pact: Gandhi vs. Ambedkar — different parties, UPSC trap
Communal Award (1932) by Ramsay MacDonald triggered Poona Pact — Gandhi-Irwin pact's failure at RTC indirectly caused Communal Award
Both pacts involved Gandhi's personal authority overriding collective INC decision-making
Poona Pact on separate electorates for depressed classes vs. Gandhi-Irwin's silence on the issue — contrast in scope
